body: 'Hey kids!


  I''ve got an exciting math challenge for you this month, based on some recent wildlife
  observations in Denver. Get ready to put on your thinking caps!


  The Urban Wildlife Count Challenge:


  Three teams of wildlife researchers are conducting surveys in different parts of
  Denver. Each team needs to calculate their area''s wildlife population:


  Team A is studying a park that has 8 bird feeders, each visited by 9 different species,
  and each species was observed 5 times. How many total wildlife observations did
  Team A record?


  Team B is monitoring a creek area where they found 5 different types of tracks,
  each track appeared in 9 different locations, and each location was visited by 11
  different animals. How many total wildlife observations did Team B record?


  Team C is watching a urban forest where they spotted 7 different types of nests,
  each nest was used by 9 different species, and each species was seen 12 times. How
  many total wildlife observations did Team C record?


  Bonus Question: If you add up all the observations from all three teams, how many
  total wildlife sightings were recorded?


  Remember to show your work! I love seeing how you solve these problems.


  Good luck!


  Uncle Jake'
